definitions.explanation: Describing people who get along well and have a warm, close relationship. A colloquial i-adjective related to the noun {仲良|なかよ}し.

examples.japanese: ⟦{二人|ふたり}→二人：00622_futari⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦とても→とても：00593_totemo⟧{仲良|なかよ}い。
examples.english: The two of them are very close.

examples.japanese: ⟦{兄弟|きょうだい}→兄弟：00964_kyoudai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{仲良|なかよ}い⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧ことだ。
examples.english: It's a good thing when siblings are on good terms.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{学生|がくせい}→学生：00610_gakusei⟧⟦{時代|じだい}→時代：01424_jidai⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦ずっと→ずっと：00912_zutto⟧{仲良|なかよ}く⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: I've been on good terms with her ever since our student days.

notes:
A colloquial i-adjective meaning that people get along well. Built from ⟦{仲|なか}→仲：09513_naka⟧ (relationship) + ⟦{良|よ}い→良い：02350_yoi⟧ (good).

USAGE:
- The more standard ways to say this are ⟦{仲|なか}→仲：09513_naka⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧ / ⟦{仲|なか}→仲：09513_naka⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧よい (with が) and the set phrase ⟦{仲|なか}→仲：09513_naka⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧. {仲良|なかよ}い as a single word is common in casual speech and writing.
- The adverbial {仲良|なかよ}く is very common: ⟦{仲良|なかよ}くする→仲良くする：25567_nakayokusuru⟧ (to get along), {仲良|なかよ}く⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧ (to become friends).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{仲良|なかよ}し→仲良し：11449_nakayoshi⟧: a close friend; being close — the noun form, also used as a na-adjective
- ⟦{親|した}しい→親しい：02345_shitashii⟧: close, intimate — emphasizes depth of a personal bond rather than simply getting along
